issue.title: Require immutable event revisions as workflow acquisition sources
issue.body:
## Problem

The current YAML guide requires a privileged workflow to verify the fetched commit after acquisition. It does not require an immutable event revision as the acquisition source.

A run can fetch `github.ref` after another event moves that ref. The later comparison with `github.sha` detects the mismatch but cannot recover the event commit. The run then fails although the immutable event commit remains valid and retrievable.

## Deferral rationale and trigger

PR #174 did not receive authorization for another protected guide edit. Start this work only after a maintainer explicitly authorizes `.github/instructions/yaml.instructions.md` and the exact rule scope in a new implementation task.

This issue does not provide that authorization. It does not start implementation.

## Affected scope

The future rule applies to GitHub Actions jobs that claim to validate one immutable event commit. It includes privileged `pull_request_target` jobs and similar jobs that fetch or check out Git data.

Keep least privilege, non-forcing fetches, bounded acquisition, and exact post-acquisition commit verification. Do not change the completed workflow repair through this guide task.

## Origin and implemented workflow

- Candidate PR: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174
- Origin thread: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174#discussion_r3834358343
- Disposition reply: https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/pull/174#discussion_r3834638076
- Implemented workflow commit: `00d380586bb728544bad921f1ab809d49646a89b`
- Implemented workflow tree: `9dbea0305812650d4143df6f8cba8f195881fc12`
- Implemented workflow path: `.github/workflows/devcontainer-ci.yml`

PR #174 already fixes the workflow at the recorded commit and tree. This issue tracks only future guide work.

## Examples

Compliant acquisition uses the immutable event revision as the fetch source.

```yaml
env:
  EXPECTED_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
```

```sh
git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin \
  "${EXPECTED_REVISION}:refs/remotes/event/target"
actual_revision="$(git rev-parse --verify 'refs/remotes/event/target^{commit}')"
test "$actual_revision" = "$EXPECTED_REVISION"
```

Noncompliant acquisition resolves a mutable ref first and compares the result later.

```yaml
env:
  EXPECTED_REF: ${{ github.ref }}
  EXPECTED_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
```

```sh
git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin \
  "${EXPECTED_REF}:refs/remotes/event/target"
actual_revision="$(git rev-parse --verify 'refs/remotes/event/target^{commit}')"
test "$actual_revision" = "$EXPECTED_REVISION"
```

The final comparison is necessary, but it is insufficient when acquisition resolves a mutable ref. It detects the race after acquisition instead of preventing it.

## Acceptance and validation

- [ ] State that an immutable event revision must be the fetch or checkout source.
- [ ] Prohibit mutable-ref acquisition followed only by expected-revision comparison.
- [ ] Preserve the least-privilege, no-force, bounded-fetch, and exact-commit rules.
- [ ] Include one compliant immutable-revision example and one noncompliant mutable-ref example.
- [ ] Record explicit maintainer authorization before changing `.github/instructions/yaml.instructions.md`.
- [ ] Update the guide version and date as its instructions require.
- [ ] Add a ref-move validation fixture that proves immutable acquisition remains deterministic.
- [ ] Verify `.github/workflows/devcontainer-ci.yml` conforms at the recorded commit and tree.
- [ ] Run repository instruction validation, Markdown validation, front-matter YAML parsing, and two clean full pre-commit passes.
- [ ] Record exact commands, native exits, changed paths, Git objects, bytes, and SHA-256 values.

Do not assign this issue, attach it to a project, create a relationship, or link a branch during creation.
issue.display_title: Require immutable event revisions as workflow acquisition sources
